label: maxturns3-oneread-opus-high
claude_args: --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --max-turns 3 --add-dir ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-review --add-dir ${{ github.workspace }}/../../_actions --setting-sources user --disallowedTools "Bash,Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,WebFetch,WebSearch,Read(//proc/**),Read(**/.git/**)" --json-schema '{"type": "object", "required": ["summary", "findings"], "additionalProperties": false, "properties": { "summary": {"type": "string"}, "findings": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "required": ["path", "line", "body"], "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "line": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1000000}, "body": {"type": "string"}}}}}}'
prompt:
You are reviewing pull request #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} as a code reviewer.
The PR's head is checked out in the working directory. Its diff against the base
branch is in ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-review/pr.diff.

You get exactly one turn of reads, then you must answer: a second turn of reads
leaves no turn for the answer, and the review is lost. In that one turn, make all
your Read calls in parallel: the diff, every source file it touches, the unchanged
code the change calls or is called by that you expect to matter, and AGENTS.md or
CLAUDE.md where present. Skip generated files, lockfiles, snapshots and recorded
data. Then answer from what you have read; don't read again.

Your review may be the only one this PR gets before it merges on its own, so be
thorough. For each change, ask what happens on the paths the author didn't test:
another event or trigger, a rerun, a skipped or cancelled job, a different actor
(a bot, an app, a person without write access), an empty, malformed or unusual
input (whitespace, tabs, Unicode, markup), a race between two runs. For GitHub
Actions workflows and merge gates, reason about how GitHub itself behaves: which
events fire, what a skipped or failed check does to a PR's mergeStateStatus, who
the actor is, what each token can do. The source of the actions this review runs on
is under ${{ github.workspace }}/../../_actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>; read it when a
pinned action's behaviour decides the answer. Where the behaviour of an action or
of GitHub decides it and you can't check it here, say what you're relying on.
Look hardest at code that decides whether something merges, releases or gets
permissions, and at text processing that turns input into rendered output.

Report every real problem a maintainer would want fixed or knowingly accepted
before merging: bugs, security issues, broken edge cases, missing or wrong tests,
and clear departures from the repository's conventions. Don't report style nits,
praise, or the PR's scope (what it bundles together is the author's call).

Every finding names a file path relative to the repository root and a line number
on the new side of that file, on a line the diff adds or shows as context: a finding
anywhere else holds the merge until the next push. When the problem lies in code the
diff doesn't touch, put the finding on the changed line that calls it, depends on it
or should have changed with it. Before you report a line, read it in the checked-out
file (not in the diff) and make sure it is the line the finding is about. Say what
goes wrong, in which situation, and how to fix it.

Answer with a short summary of the change and your verdict, and your findings.

review.summary: The PR removes `.WithHealthCheck(name)` from the MongoDB and Redis AppHost extensions. `AddMongoDB` and `AddRedis` already register and attach their own health check, so the extra annotation pointed at an unregistered key and AppHost failed at startup with "A health check registration is missing". It also adds the dashboard/OTLP endpoint variables and `ASPIRE_ALLOW_UNSECURED_TRANSPORT` to the http launch profile, adds a regression test per extension, and re-indents the MongoDB tests with tabs. The production changes look correct. The two new regression tests, though, probably pass with or without the fix: they build a ServiceProvider from `builder.Services` without calling `builder.Build()`, and they only reject `OptionsValidationException`. Any other exception, such as the validator failing to resolve `DistributedApplicationModel`, passes silently. They don't guard the fix and should be tightened before merging. I couldn't run the tests or read the Aspire source here; the reasoning relies on how I remember Aspire.Hosting 9.x registering its health-check validator.

findings.body:
This regression test probably can't fail, so it doesn't protect the fix.

It builds a provider with `builder.Services.BuildServiceProvider()` and never calls `builder.Build()`. As I recall Aspire.Hosting (I couldn't check its source here), the missing-health-check validator is an `IValidateOptions<HealthCheckServiceOptions>` whose factory needs `DistributedApplicationModel`. That type is only registered inside `Build()`. Without it, resolving `IOptions<HealthCheckServiceOptions>.Value` throws `InvalidOperationException` (no service for `DistributedApplicationModel`) before any validation runs.

`NotThrow<OptionsValidationException>()` only fails on that exact type, so the test passes whether or not `.WithHealthCheck(name)` is present. It also accepts any other startup exception. That goes against CLAUDE.md's "Write the failing test first … for bug fixes".

Fix: `using DistributedApplication app = builder.Build();`, resolve `app.Services.GetRequiredService<IOptions<HealthCheckServiceOptions>>().Value`, and assert `act.Should().NotThrow();`. `Build()` doesn't start containers. Then confirm the test fails with `.WithHealthCheck(name)` restored in `RedisExtensions`.

Same problem as the Redis test: this one probably passes with or without the fix.

`builder.Services.BuildServiceProvider()` (line 149) skips `builder.Build()`, which is where Aspire registers the `DistributedApplicationModel` its health-check validator depends on (from memory of Aspire.Hosting; not verified here). Reading `.Value` therefore most likely throws `InvalidOperationException`, and `NotThrow<OptionsValidationException>()` ignores that. Re-adding `.WithHealthCheck(name)` to `AddMongoDBWithManagement` would not turn this test red. Any other startup failure would also be hidden.

Fix: build the app (`using DistributedApplication app = builder.Build();`), resolve the options from `app.Services`, assert `act.Should().NotThrow();`, and confirm the test fails against the old code.
